answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a ferrous-hard stake of real value before it can trade, so spinning up thousands of fake agents costs thousands of stakes. Reputation then grows slowly like a juniper, earned through verified work over time rather than bought overnight. A raven-like network of independent peers randomly re-checks claims, and any identity caught lying loses its stake and history. Faking scale becomes expensive, slow, and easy to catch.
